masks.method: Reconstruction. The six colour clusters of content.peel (k-means on the Met photograph of JP1847) were smoothed by a majority filter; each colour block's area was then grown only where a darker cluster will cover it (pale 15 px, grey 10 px, beige 7 px, lighter blue 5 px, at 1600 px wide), as if each lighter block were cut generously under the darker ones. The key line is the black-hat (thin dark strokes) of the photograph's luminance plus its darkest pixels, specks under 14 px removed. Packed as lossless RGB WebP, one block per channel.

blocks.label: Pale washes in the sky and sea

day.label: typical
day.line: One printer could pull about two hundred sheets a day.

keyproof.caption: A real key-block proof: Utagawa (Gountei) Sadahide, Proof Line-Block Print for Fan, 19th century. The Metropolitan Museum of Art 2007.49.284, CC0. The notches outside the picture are kentō.

sources.t: Asian Art Museum, “The ukiyo-e woodblock printing process”: the drawing pasted face down on cherry wood; one block per colour, each with kentō; damp paper rubbed with a baren; about 200 prints a day; at least about ten impressions
sources.conf: documented (process); probable (the day’s count, a typical figure)

sources.t: The Met, “The Great Wave: Anatomy of an Icon”: spectroscopy finds Prussian blue mixed with indigo in the dark stripes, and pure Prussian blue printed twice in the hollow
